narrative:
The model estimates you have a 13% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a high probability, it is enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. First, you have had no past class failures, which is exactly the same as the average for students who passed; this strongly pulls the prediction toward passing. Second, you have a clear desire to pursue higher education, matching 100% of students who succeeded; this also pushes the outcome noticeably toward passing. However, your father’s education level, which is only primary school, works in the opposite direction. Among students who passed, far more had parents with secondary or higher education. This background factor is the main element that tips the model toward expecting you might struggle, outweighing the protective effects of your clean record and ambition.

To improve, focus on what you can control now. Since family educational support at home is limited, seek extra help from teachers, study groups, or the remedial courses themselves. Even small, consistent increases in study time and making the most of your internet access for learning resources could close the gap the model has identified. Taking these steps early gives you the best chance of turning the 13% risk into a clear pass.
